Exact edge-overlap counting gives c(A-E mu^2), which equals the stated ambiguity dispersion. Weyl orthogonality and u^2<=u give both endpoints, with equality characterized by SIC and maximal isotropic stabilizer subgroups. In prime dimension >=5, a nondegenerate quadratic Gauss sum gives Alltop off-translation ambiguity 1/p. Numerical checks are supplementary to the complete proof; no unverified infinite claim rests on finite enumeration.

value.rationale: This is an exact all-dimensional sampling-statistic law for Fourier/Gabor frame robustness: the entire random-erasure fluctuation depends on just one natural Fourier ambiguity flatness functional. Sharp attainable maximum and conditional zero minimum have rigid and distinct geometric equality cases (stabilizer vs SIC); prime Alltop windows reduce maximal variance by p^2. The distinction provides a meaningful exact metric for designing redundant Fourier measurements under random erasure, without falsely converting a Frobenius fluctuation into a condition-number result.
